title: Settings
description: Account, team, and integrations. Host components (proxy, servers, swarm, disk) live in the Infrastructure group.

validation.chatIdNumeric: Chat ID must be a number
validation.urlHttp: URL must start with http:// or https://
validation.certAndKeyRequired: Certificate and private key are required

expiry.daysLeft: {days, plural, one {# day left} other {# days left}}

twoFactor.title: Two-factor authentication (2FA)
twoFactor.description: A TOTP code from an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Aegis, 1Password, …) is required at every sign-in. API tokens are not affected.

setup.title: Enable 2FA
setup.description: Scan this QR code with an authenticator app, then enter the 6-digit code it shows.

backup.title: 2FA is on — save your backup codes
backup.description: Each code works only once, to sign in when you don't have your authenticator. They will not be shown again.

disableDialog.title: Disable 2FA?
disableDialog.description: Enter your password to confirm. The secret and backup codes will be deleted.

tokens.title: API token
tokens.description: Personal access tokens for CI/CLI — they act as your account (same role). Use as Authorization: Bearer aoox_…. Endpoint documentation:
tokens.scopeHelp: With no selection: the token sees every project you can see and may use platform settings. With a selection: only those projects, and platform settings (registry, servers, proxy, swarm, notifications) are refused.

created.title: Token created
created.description: Copy it now — the token will not be shown again. Only its hash is stored.

members.title: Members
members.description: All members see all projects. Owners/admins manage platform components; only the owner changes roles.
members.setPasswordPrompt: New password for {email} (min. 8 characters). Tell them in person.
members.disable2faDescription: This account will be protected by its password only, which is less secure, and its backup codes stop working. The owner of the account can enable 2FA again from the Account page.
members.deleteDescription: The account is deleted permanently: it can no longer sign in and its membership in every project is removed. This cannot be undone.

invite.title: Invite a member
invite.description: The invitation link is valid for 7 days and is shown only once — send it to them yourself.
invite.noOrigin: WEB_ORIGIN is not set on the API, so only the token is available; open {path} on this web app.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Deploy started/succeeded/failed, backup failed, and container down, sent to Telegram, Slack, Discord, email, or webhook. Tokens are stored encrypted.

hints.telegram: Create a bot via @BotFather, add it to the group/chat, then enter the token and chat ID (groups are usually negative).
hints.slack: An Incoming Webhook from a Slack app (https://hooks.slack.com/services/…).
hints.webhook: Your own endpoint; it receives a JSON POST (title, level, event, …).
hints.email: Your SMTP server (e.g. Gmail app password, Mailgun, SES). Port 465 = implicit TLS; 587 = STARTTLS.

dialog.title: New notification channel
dialog.secretHelp: When set, every delivery carries X-Aoox-Signature: sha256=HMAC(secret, body) (plus X-Aoox-Event and X-Aoox-Delivery) — verify it like a GitHub webhook.
dialog.secretsNote: The token/URL cannot be viewed again after saving.

gitCredentials.title: Git credentials
gitCredentials.description: HTTPS tokens for private repos. Stored encrypted and used only when Docker clones the repo.
gitCredentials.empty: No credentials yet — every repo is cloned anonymously.

hints.github: Personal access token (classic: repo scope; fine-grained: Contents read). Any username works, e.g. x-access-token.
hints.gitlab: Deploy token (Settings<arrow></arrow>Repository<arrow></arrow>Deploy tokens, scope read_repository) — enter the token's username.
hints.generic: Username + HTTPS password/token from your git server.

gitCredentials.tokenHelp: Cannot be viewed again after saving.

secretConnections.title: Secret manager
secretConnections.description: Connections to Infisical (machine identity). Applications can pull secrets from it when the container is created, without copying them into env. The client secret is stored encrypted and cannot be viewed again.
secretConnections.empty: No connections yet — applications use plain env.
secretConnections.dialogDescription: Create a machine identity (Universal Auth) in Infisical, give it read access to the projects you need, then enter its Client ID and Client secret here.
secretConnections.urlHelp: Leave empty for Infisical Cloud; fill in for a self-hosted instance.
secretConnections.secretHelp: Cannot be viewed again after saving.

backupDestinations.title: Backup destinations (S3)
backupDestinations.description: S3-compatible buckets (AWS, MinIO, R2, Backblaze, …) where database backup copies are sent. Choose one per database in its Backup tab.
backupDestinations.empty: No destinations yet — backups are kept only on this server's volume.
backupDestinations.dialogDescription: Credentials are stored encrypted and used only by the uploader container (rclone). The bucket must already exist.
backupDestinations.secretHelp: Cannot be viewed again after saving.
backupDestinations.pathStyle: Path-style (host/bucket) — required for MinIO, safe for the others

certificates.title: SSL certificates
certificates.description: Your own certificates (corporate CA, purchased wildcard, Cloudflare Origin CA) for application domains, instead of Let's Encrypt. The private key is stored encrypted and cannot be viewed again.
certificates.empty: No certificates yet — HTTPS domains use Let's Encrypt automatically.
certificates.deleteInUse: This certificate is still used by {count, plural, one {# domain} other {# domains}}, so it cannot be deleted. Move the domains to another certificate or Let's Encrypt first.
certificates.deleteDescription: The certificate and its private key are deleted permanently from aoox. This cannot be undone.
certificates.usedBy: used by {count, plural, one {# domain} other {# domains}}
certificates.dialogReplaceDescription: Replace the certificate content with a new one (e.g. a renewal). The name stays, and every domain that uses it must remain covered.
certificates.dialogUploadDescription: Paste or choose a PEM file. The certificate may contain a chain (leaf then intermediates); the private key must not be passphrase-protected.
certificates.keyHelp: Cannot be viewed again after saving.

pem.certificate: The certificate must be a PEM block starting with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----.
pem.encryptedKey: Encrypted (passphrase-protected) private keys are not supported. Remove the passphrase first.
pem.key: The private key must be a PEM block starting with -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- (or RSA/EC PRIVATE KEY).

audit.title: Audit log
audit.description: Every request that changes something (and sign-in attempts), who made it and how. Kept for 90 days.
